samples.summary: No test covers comment edit/delete (and its author-only authorization) on the flat-root document types (doc / pdf)
samples.evidence: `describe('ApiV1CommentsController on other document types')` (spec lines ~326-380) only exercises `list`, `reply` and `setResolved` on a `doc` root. The whole non-sheet branch of `mutateMap` (comments.controller.ts, the `withDocument<void, FlatCommentRoot>` path that calls `authorize?.(doc.getRoot().comments)` and then `mutate(root.comments)`) is never exercised for `deleteThread`, `deleteComment` or `editComment`. Every authorship test lives under `describe('edit / delete authorship')`, whose `seededThread()` uses `harness('sheet', sheetRoot())`. If the flat-root branch stopped calling `authorize` (or called it with the wrong map), the suite would stay green while any workspace member could delete or rewrite another user's comments on a word-processor document or a PDF — the exact guard the controller docblock says it added because the editor only enforces it client-side.
searchedFor: grep for ForbiddenException / deleteComment / editComment in comments.controller.spec.ts
grep for 'pdf' and 'doc' harness usages in the spec
glob packages/backend/src/api/v1/*.spec.ts for another comments spec

samples.summary: 'keeps a concurrent edit to another slide' cannot fail if the controller replaced the whole slides array — the exact regression it claims to guard
samples.evidence: The test captures `untouched = slides()[0]` and `peerEdit = { ...untouched.elements[0] }`, calls `controller.add`, then asserts `expect(slides()[0]).toBe(untouched)` and `elements[0]).toEqual(peerEdit)`. No concurrent write is simulated, and a whole-array assignment (`root.slides = [...old, newSlide]`) — the last-write-wins failure the docblock says these verbs exist to avoid — copies element references, so `slides()[0]` would still be the very same object and both assertions would still pass. The granularity property is only genuinely covered in slide-ops.spec.ts ('carries only the new slide, never a replacement deck' and the peer-insert `insert-after` test); this controller-level test adds no signal despite its name.

samples.summary: The route-collision guard has no sanity assertion that any routes were enumerated, so it passes vacuously if handler metadata stops being readable
samples.evidence: The spec builds `seen`/`collisions` from `Reflect.getMetadata(PATH_METADATA, handler)` and ends with `expect(collisions).toEqual([])` (line 78). If the metadata key or extraction ever stops matching (Nest upgrade, decorators applied differently, handlers not on the prototype), every handler is skipped by `if (suffix === undefined) continue;` and the assertion still passes. Only `controllers.length >= 18` is asserted (line 42), which guards controller enumeration, not route enumeration. This spec is the only test guarding the shadowing behaviour this diff reacts to (tab reorder moved from `:tabId/move` to `:tabId/reorder`), and there is no positive case proving the detector actually detects a collision.
searchedFor: grep PATH_METADATA across packages/backend/src (only this file)

samples.summary: No test for an unknown layoutId on the new POST /slides endpoint, which silently falls back to the first built-in layout
samples.evidence: `addSlide` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, whose `resolveLayout` does `this.doc.layouts.find(...) ?? getLayout(layoutId)`, and `getLayout` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196) returns `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` for any unrecognised id. So `slides slide add --layout typo` silently creates a slide with a different layout than requested and returns 200. Neither slide-ops.spec.ts ('addSlide' block only uses 'title-body' and 'blank') nor slides.controller.spec.ts ('add' block) passes an unknown layout id, and the controller has no validation, so neither the refusal nor the fallback is pinned by any test.

samples.summary: The new HttpClient methods' URLs are never exercised; the CLI test mocks HttpClient wholesale and the dry-run literals are a second, independent spelling of the same paths
samples.evidence: class-b-commands.test.ts replaces the entire `HttpClient` class with a stub (`vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js', ...)`, lines ~52-75), so `listComments`, `createCommentThread`, `moveTab` ('/reorder'), `addSlide`, `setWorksheetImages`, `getBoardContent` etc. are asserted only by argument, never by the URL they build. packages/cli/test/http-client-paths.test.ts (the only place real URLs are checked against a mocked `fetch`) covers getDocument/getCells/listTabs/getDocContent/api-keys and none of the new methods. The dry-run previews in tabs.ts/comments.ts/slides-edit.ts/sheets-images.ts hard-code the path a second time, and only two of them (tab duplicate, board set-content) have a dry-run URL assertion — so a typo in, say, `moveTab`'s `/reorder` path would ship with the whole CLI suite green.
searchedFor: grep for moveTab / listComments in packages/cli/test

samples.summary: Nothing asserts the HTTP path of the new backend routes; controller specs invoke the methods directly
samples.evidence: tabs.controller.spec.ts calls `controller.move(...)` directly, so the `@Post(':tabId/reorder')` decorator value — the whole point of the docblock explaining why it is not `move` — is never asserted. Same for `ApiV1SlidesController` (`slides`, `slides/:slideId/move`, `layouts`), `ApiV1CommentsController` and `ApiV1WorksheetImagesController`: their specs construct the class and call methods. Only route-collision.spec.ts touches PATH_METADATA, and it only checks for duplicates. Renaming a decorator path would leave the backend suite green while the CLI (which posts to the literal `/reorder`) 404s.

samples.summary: duplicateTab's carry-over of the non-sheet tab metadata fields (kind, datasourceId, query) is untested
samples.evidence: `duplicateTab` explicitly copies `source.kind`, `source.datasourceId` and `source.query` onto the new `TabMeta` (tab-ops.ts lines ~163-166). tab-ops.spec.ts's `describe('duplicateTab')` covers only the name uniquing, the tabOrder position, cell carry-over and comment dropping; no fixture sets any of those three fields, so dropping them would go unnoticed. (`applyDelete`'s `if (root.sheets?.[tabId])` guard for a worksheet-less datasource tab is likewise never exercised — every delete test uses a sheet tab.)

samples.summary: applySlideChange's 'insert-after with a vanished source' fallback (append) is untested
samples.evidence: `case 'insert-after'` falls back to `slides.length` when `findIndex` returns -1 — i.e. a peer deleted the source slide between the read and the write, and the copy is appended rather than lost. slide-ops.spec.ts covers the analogous vanished-slide case for `remove` ('is a no-op when the slide is already gone at apply time') and for `move` implicitly, but the `insert-after` miss path has no test; the duplicate tests always keep the source present.

samples.summary: The stdin branch of `sheets images set` is untested
samples.evidence: The command reads the payload from `process.stdin` when `--data` is absent (sheets-images.ts lines ~66-78), including the 'Invalid JSON image data on stdin' message. class-b-commands.test.ts only drives the `--data` branch ('accepts the envelope its own get prints' and the malformed-payload case), and no other CLI test registers this command, so the stdin read and its error wording are never executed.

samples.summary: The board GET test mocks the Yorkie callback away, so readBoardRoot never runs in it
samples.evidence: `yorkieService.withDocument.mockResolvedValue(board)` means the controller's `(doc) => readBoardRoot(doc.getRoot())` callback is never invoked; the assertion `expect(await controller.getContent(...)).toEqual(board)` just re-asserts the mock's return value plus the options object. This matches the pre-existing pattern for docs/slides/note in the same file, and `readBoardRoot` is covered independently in board-tree.spec.ts, so the loss is only that the wiring between the two is untested.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence independently. comments.controller.ts:546-585 has two distinct branches in mutateMap, with a separate authorize call site for the flat root (line 578) used by doc/pdf. In comments.controller.spec.ts, every deleteThread/deleteComment/editComment invocation is under 'edit / delete authorship' (453-539) whose seededThread() (459-476) uses harness('sheet', sheetRoot()); the PDF describe (306-353) only calls createThread, the 'other document types' describe (355-405) only calls list/reply/setResolved, and the doc-rooted notification tests (570-630) only call reply. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths for a counterexample: a repo-wide grep for ApiV1CommentsController shows only api-v1.module.ts, the controller and this single spec reference it, so no other test can exercise the controller; the backend e2e suites (packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts) contain no comment-route coverage (only document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts:47,66,123 touching comment data); and packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts:260-334 exercises `comments delete`/`delete-comment` only against a mocked HTTP client. Blocking under this lens: the author-only guard on doc/pdf edit/delete has no test at all, so removing or misrouting the authorize call in the flat-root branch would keep the suite green while any workspace member could delete or rewrite another user's comments.
